title: Graphing the Square Root of the Absolute Value Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = sqrt(|x|) by writing it in piecewise form and using symmetry.

steps.title: Write y = sqrt(|x|) in Piecewise Form
steps.explanation: For x >= 0, |x| = x so y = sqrt(x). For x < 0, |x| = -x > 0 so y = sqrt(-x), which is the reflection of y = sqrt(x) across the y-axis.
steps.why: Splitting |x| at x = 0 decomposes y = sqrt(|x|) into two symmetric square root branches.

steps.title: Determine the Domain, Range, and Even Symmetry
steps.explanation: Because |x| >= 0 for all real x, the square root is defined on the entire real line (-infinity, infinity) with range [0, infinity) and even symmetry across the y-axis.
steps.why: The absolute value ensures a non-negative radicand for every real number x.

steps.title: Describe the Cusp at the Origin and Key Points
steps.explanation: The two square root branches meet at a sharp vertical cusp at (0, 0) and rise concavely outward in the first and second quadrants through (+/-1, 1) and (+/-4, 2).
steps.why: Both branches have vertical tangents at x = 0, forming a symmetric cusp at the origin.
